questions.question: Name and explain five qualities of a good manager, with an example of each from a supermarket.
questions.expected_answer: Any five: integrity/honesty (keeps promises, follows own rules); fairness (no favouritism, same rules for all); communication (clear instructions, listens, gives feedback respectfully); decision-making (gathers facts, decides on time, owns mistakes); motivation and development (recognises good work, trains, delegates); organisation and time management (plans, sets priorities); flexibility and problem-solving (adapts to outages or rushes, looks for solutions not blame); calmness under pressure; knowledge of the work; vision.

questions.question: Explain technical, human and conceptual skills and how the mix changes between lower, middle and top management. Then compare the autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire styles, giving a situation suited to each.
questions.expected_answer: Technical: doing/knowing the specific work (most needed by supervisors). Human: working with and motivating people (needed at all levels). Conceptual: seeing the whole business and long-term (most needed by top management). Moving up: technical decreases, conceptual increases. Autocratic: manager decides alone; suits emergencies/new workers. Democratic: workers consulted, manager decides; suits planning when there is time and workers have knowledge. Laissez-faire: workers decide how; suits skilled, motivated experts.

questions.question: Team A (8 people) lost 1 worker in a year; Team B (8 people) lost 4. Calculate each team's staff turnover, explain why high turnover is costly, and give one reason that would not indicate poor management.
questions.expected_answer: Team A: 1 ÷ 8 = 12.5%. Team B: 4 ÷ 8 = 50%. Costly: recruitment, interviewing and training costs; lost experience; more mistakes while new staff learn. Not poor management: promotions, studying, relocation, retirement, seasonal contracts, or a competitor paying more.
